From: Alex Reid <alex.reid@cardiomed.com>

Cc: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@cardiomed.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transfer mechanisms + subprocessor evidence for Redwood DPA

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before we start legal signoff we need to get our transfer and subprocessor housekeeping in order. Two specific asks from Legal/Procurement: 

1) A short mapping that shows how Redwood intends to satisfy EU transfer requirements for CardioMed: SCCs, UK IDTA/UK addendum, and whether a TIA/DTIA is used for specific processing nodes. We need the mapping by environment (hosted, dedicated, private) and whether fallback routing could route data outside EU/UK.

2) A CSV of active subprocessors and the evidence each one can provide (SCC attachment, SOC2, onshore proxying, HSM/KMS residency). Procurement prefers a single file we can attach to the DPA appendix.

Can you share those artifacts and a short note on any outstanding gaps we should expect? If we can get this by EOD Wednesday (our deadline for the internal security review), that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alex Reid
Head of Procurement
CardioMed Solutions

Attachment: none

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reid <alex.reid@cardiomed.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@cardiomed.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transfer mechanisms + subprocessor evidence for Redwood DPA

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. I attached three artifacts that should cover the items you requested:

- Redwood_SCCs_mapping_v1.pdf — mapping doc showing: which standard SCC modules we rely on, per-environment controls, and our recommended clause for cross-border fallback.
- UK_Addendum_TIA_matrix.xlsx — matrix that shows when we apply the UK addendum vs an internal TIA for edge processing in the UK.
- subprocessor_list_cardio_med.csv — current list of active subprocessors and short evidence tags (SOC2 / SCCs / HSM available).

Short notes on gaps / exceptions:
- Hosted API: default flows use SCCs for EU exports with our subprocessors; in very rare failover cases requests may route to non-EU compute for latency reasons — we enumerate those in the mapping and propose contractual fallback (geo-preferences + explicit routing SLO).
- Dedicated: customer can lock to EU-only Dedicated pools; that resolves transfer concerns but requires a committed capacity order.
- Private: deploys within customer VPC/on-prem — transfers are controlled by the customer.

Outstanding evidence items (we flagged in the CSV):
- One edge caching partner (EdgeCacheCo) has SOC2 but cannot provide HSM residency; we propose a compensating control (encrypted KV with customer-managed keys).
- Two small telemetry processors can provide SCC attachments but need a short attestation on retention (we can push a signed attestation).

If you want, I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Legal this week to talk through the mapping and the DocuSign appendix language.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SCCs_mapping_v1.pdf, UK_Addendum_TIA_matrix.xlsx, subprocessor_list_cardio_med.csv

Subject: Internal: CardioMed — need quick confirmations on evidence items

Team —

Alex at CardioMed asked for mapping + subprocessor CSV (sent) but Legal pushed back on a couple of evidence gaps. Please see the items below and reply with the exact artifact we can provide by Wed EOD: 

1) EdgeCacheCo (edge cache partner) — SOC2 yes; HSM residency NO. Laura, can we produce the customer-managed KMS flow doc and a short note on how KM rotation works? We should include key-escrow options for Dedicated.

2) TelemetryVendorX & TelemetryVendorY — both can sign SCC attachments but they need a retention attestation that we control. Marissa, can you draft a one-paragraph attestation template and confirm who will sign?

3) Routing fallback — CardioMed cares about non-EU fallback during bursts. Jonas, can you confirm whether we have a configurable route pin for EU-only at the account level or if that is gated behind Dedicated? Need exact boolean and config path.

Plan: gather artifacts and send a consolidated zip + DocuSign appendix link back to CardioMed by Wed EOD. If any of you expect delays, flag now.

Thanks —
Kim

Got the artifacts, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after a quick review: 

- The SCCs mapping is helpful but they asked for a short call to validate the fallback sequence (specifically whether transient burst traffic could cross to APAC nodes). Can you confirm availability for Tue afternoon 4/20 (we're flexible 1-4pm PT)?
- The CSV is almost complete; Procurement needs a precise column that enumerates the legal artifact type per subprocessor ("SCC_attachment", "SOC2_report", "HSM_residency", or "attestation_signed"). Right now your CSV uses shorthand tags; can you expand into explicit artifact_type column?
- For the two telemetry vendors, Legal wants a signed retention attestation with a name and title. If you can provide a one-line attestation (PDF) per vendor, that will speed approval.

We can do DocuSign for the DPA once the attachments zip is finalized. PT Tue afternoon works for short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
